recipes.name: Cherry Poke Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package fruit flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (16 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Prepare and bake cake mix according to package directions for one 9x13-inch cake. Remove cake from oven. Poke holes at once down through cake with a fork. Holes should be at 1-inch intervals.
While the cake cools, combine gelatin with boiling water. Pour gelatin mixture over the cake. Top with cherry pie filling, then cover with whipped topping. Refrigerate cake for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cherry Poke Cake
raw_recipe.description: This Jell-O poke cake is topped with cherry pie filling and whipped topping for a fun, festive dessert that everyone will love.

review.reviewBody: Great cake! I do have one problem with it though.....my husband ate half of it a few hours after I made it. LOL I did change just one little thing about the recipe. I used a wooden spoon handle to make the holes instead of a fork. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

I made it a double layer cake with 2 round 8 inch cake pans. After baking the cake and adding the jello I let it sit in the fridge overnight. In the morning, I trimmed the tops of the cake then added some of the cherry and whipped cream. Added the second layer and repeat. Added strawberries and blueberries to make it festive for the 4th of July.

I made this with a chocolate cake mix, using the handle of a wooden spoon to poke the holes, and drizzled raspberry Jell-o over the warm cake. Once it cooled, I iced it with a buttercream frosting, finishing off with a zig zag of luscious raspberry curd on top. Picture perfect! Exceptionally delicious!

My mother-in-law used to make this cake. It was/is my husband's favorite. She passed before I could get the recipe so I had to search for it. So glad I found it!! The only thing she did different, is she added a layer of vanilla pudding on top before the Cool Whip. First time I made this, I didn't do that and we couldn't figure out what was missing. Finally my husband figured it out!! I use a chopstick now to poke the holes because a fork or toothpick just doesn't cut it. Chopstick works quite well. What's pictured here was made with a funfetti cake mix as that's what my daughter wanted. Yup... the kids love it too!! Kids.... they're in their 30's ha ha ha!!!

I made a peach poke cake - using a white cake mix (cut out the oil and added peach flavoured sugar-free applesauce); the jello was sugar-free peach flavour; I didn't have any peach pie filling, so the topping was made by cooking a can of fruit cocktail packed in water with 2 tablespoons of stevia and 2 tablespoons of corn starch. We served it with a squirt of real whipped cream. YUM! I can't wait to try other flavours.

I WAS searching for this thing called poke but it’s like sushi. We’re trying to cut the carbs and our young new neighbors suggested the stuff. Came across this wonderful cake instead. Never seen anything like it! Filled it with multiple colors/flavors of jell-o brand gelatin, NO COMPETITORS.

Play around with this recipe, its lots of fun. I made a chocolate cake mix (added a box of instant pudding and one egg) and baked in a 9x13. Then I poured raspberry gelatin over the top, chilled, cut in half and filled the middle layer with raspberry jelly, and frosted with dark chocolate frosting. Delicious!

I made it and loved it. I used German Chocolate cake mix and tried to pour white chocolate in the holes. It didn't work because I didn't thin it enough. Since I used a Bundt pan I put it onto a serving dish and poured Chocolate Almond Bark all over it. Ugliest cake ever, but what a treat for chocolate lovers. I took it to a house warming and got back the serving plate the next day. If one follows the recipe more closely than I it will make a great cake. Thanks for sharing the recipe .

I have made this cake twice for two clubs I am in. Got many compliments from both groups. I used a bought icing and no pie fillings, and everyone loved it. I made one a yellow cake with raspberry jello and the other a white cake with green jello for St. Patricks Day celebration.
This one has been in our family for a while. We always use yellow cake mix with strawberry jello and just whipped cream with strawberries on top. I use a chopstick for the holes too.
This was delicious! Very light and refreshing. I used strawberry Jello. Instead of using a whole can of cherry pie filling, I only used the jelled portion and not the cherries. Everyone loved it!

Love this recipe! I love cherry/almond desserts..SO,I used Pillsbury Almond cake mix & added a lil almond extract 2 the batter also. After I added the whipped cream I sprinkled some sliced almonds on top.
I Loved it. It's moist and light without being soggy. Very versatile, any fruit any Jello. Thanks

You know, for what this is, it’s tasty. Reminded me of a little Debbie jelly roll. I thought it was a bit sweet but then again it’s a dessert. With two hungry teens and a hubby with a sweet tooth I won’t get another piece tomorrow and I am ok with that. Raspberry/blackberry jello from the depths of my pantry, cherry pie filling and cool whip - yum. Thanks for the simple ingredients, really quick to put this together.
such a perfect dessert for the summer. My family loved it!

I have made this cake so many time that I have the recipe remembered by heart. I make this cake every year for my son's birthday. He's 35 now and still today he ask for it. Love the cake it so good and easy to make. I didn't change anything.
It was a hit! I poured the cherry topping in a bowl.

GREAT RESULTS!! 
The family scarfed it up and took the leftovers
When they left!! Lucky I had tried a piece 
Easy and will make again . I added a bit of van pudding powder to the frosting after reading others reviews. That is some good cream cheese frosting too!
